questions: Should the removal of URLs happen before tokenization, and does 'removing URLs' mean replacing them with nothing (deleting them) or with a space? The current regex substitution deletes them, which could merge words incorrectly (e.g., 'Visit https://example.com now' becomes 'Visit now' with no space).

The prompt says 'considering only their first occurrence in the text.' Does this mean we should count only the first occurrence of each stopword, ignoring subsequent duplicates, or does it mean we should consider stopwords only if they appear for the first time in the text (i.e., unique stopwords)? The reference solution counts all occurrences, contradicting the prompt.

What constitutes a 'word' for tokenization? The reference uses \b\w+\b, which includes underscores and digits (since \w matches [a-zA-Z0-9_]). Should we only consider alphabetic sequences? Should hyphenated words be split?
The clarification says 'Return an empty list if no stopwords are found.' Does 'found' mean after URL removal and tokenization, or before? And should the list be empty or an empty list of tuples?

The prompt says 'The capitilization need to macth the stopwords.' Does this mean stopword matching is case-sensitive? The predefined list is all lowercase, so does 'match' require exact case (so 'The' is not a stopword) or case-insensitive matching (so 'The' matches 'the')?

Should the output list be sorted in any particular order (e.g., by frequency descending, alphabetically, or order of first appearance)? The reference returns items() order which is arbitrary in Python <3.7 and insertion order in >=3.7.
Does 'first occurrence' refer to the first occurrence in the original text (before URL removal) or in the processed text (after URL removal)?

The URL regex in the reference is 'http[s]?://\S+', which matches until whitespace. Is this the intended definition? Should it handle URLs with punctuation attached (e.g., 'https://example.com.)'? The regex might include trailing punctuation.
